messages:
alex: Quick question — can we simplify the policy engine surface by introducing an explicit 'delegate' concept so runtimes can take weights/quotas offloaded? Thinking about reducing runtime-config churn and making compatibility tests simpler. Anyone tried this?

maria: Ooh interesting. Do you mean a first-class delegate node that gets a percentage weight and specific constraints (region/cost/latency)? :thinking_face:

alex: exactly. Example sketch:
```
policy:
  delegate:
    name: 'regional-affinity'
    weight: 0.2
    constraints: ['region:us-west', 'latency<100ms']
```
Would let us avoid duplicating per-route penalties.

jay: my worry: how does this interact with preemptive slots and admission control? delegate weights can't overcommit without admission hooks.

sam: +1 to jay. Also we need to preserve explainability — route decisions must surface why delegate chosen (penalty traces).

maria: agree re: explainability. Could add a 'provenance' field in the decision blob. That keeps runtime dumb but traceable.

policy-bot: sim-run:delegate-config-1799999012 — 500k simulated requests, avg cost -2.3%, p95 latency +8ms, edge cases in region saturation.

alex: thanks. So action items: (1) prototype delegate field in compiler (2) add admission hook spec (3) decision provenance schema. Volunteers? @maria @jay

maria: I can pick up (1) and (3) — will put a small RFC + example patch.

jay: I'll take (2), will stub admission hook API with a minimal contract (sync call + capacity token return).

sam: We should also add a telemetry flag to opt-in for early experiments so we can monitor regressions.

alex: agreed. I'll open a tracking ticket and link RFCs. Nice — this keeps policy DSL compact and runtime compatibility easier. :rocket:
